messages:
jamie: seeing a spike of container restarts on prod-gpu-03, node flapping repeatedly. multiple pods OOM/killed and a lot of CUDA illegal memory access in the container logs. paging pressure looks high. anyone oncall?

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED (sev=P1) — prod:gpu-serving - CUDA illegal memory access + node flapping. Auto-assigning oncall.

priya: I'm oncall, jumping in. thanks for the heads up jamie. which models affected / any customer 503s?

jamie: several model-worker pods for embedder-v2 and chat-medium restarted. customer telemetry shows ~3% 500s for org:acme and intermittent latency spikes.

max: grabbing logs and dmesg from the node now. here's the kernel log excerpt from prod-gpu-03: 
```
[ 1123.457890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1123.457895] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, Ch 0000000a, intr 10000000. 
[ 1123.457900] kernel: CUDA: illegal memory access at 0x7f8c1b2b4000
[ 1123.457912] kernel: device 0000:3b:00.0: unhandled page fault on GPU access, address=0x7f8c1b2b4000
[ 1123.457923] oom_kill: kill process 4589 (python) score 987 or sacrifice child
```
and container stdout: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "server.py", line 412, in handle_request
    out = model.generate(batch)
RuntimeError: cuMemAlloc failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
```

lucy: that looks like a GPU driver / kernel race during KV cache reload under memory pressure. might be the same reproduction as earlier but not identical. what driver/kernel versions on node?

jamie: prod-gpu-03: nvidia-driver 525.85, kernel 6.1.12, last reboot ~2h ago (patch window).

priya: immediate mitigation plan (short):
- cordon prod-gpu-03 to stop new pods landing: `kubectl cordon prod-gpu-03`
- drain non-critical workloads off the node with `kubectl drain prod-gpu-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
- scale down batch/large-batch routes and flip affected routes to CPU-fallback model variant (edge config)
- enable per-model fallback: `route-config set --model embedder-v2 --fallback cpu-embedder-v2`

max: doing cordon now. running `kubectl get pods -o wide -n inference | grep prod-gpu-03` to identify remaining pods.

deploy-bot: cordon command executed by max at 2026-03-17T09:04:02Z.

max: drain started, migrating pods. a couple of pods keep crashing during preStop because they hit OOM before graceful shutdown. we should avoid automatic restarts for affected deployments while we triage.

priya: patching the deployment to set `spec.template.spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds=5` and `spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable=100%` to force fast evacuation for these nodes.

lucy: proposing longer-term workaround: revert recent kernel update on the affected node pool to the previous stable kernel (6.0.x) and hold patch until driver/kernel vendor confirms root cause. also consider upgrading nvidia-driver to 535.x where a similar bug was fixed.

jamie: customer impact summary for CS: org:acme + org:oro briefly saw 500s and elevated latency between 08:58-09:06 UTC while we started cordon/drain. estimated affected requests ~0.8% of total. will post note to #support and ping cs.

cs-notify: pinged support + created ticket INC-13094 for customer communications.

max: while draining, I captured node memory/pagemap stats and pod cgroup logs. looks like rapid page reclaim + GPU mmap churn. dumping relevant metrics to shared gist: https://internal.gists.redwood/6854321000/gpu-mmap-dump

priya: good. next steps:
- finish draining node and keep it cordoned.
- remove node from autoscaling pool to avoid new replacements landing in same pool.
- run driver repro on an isolated test node: reproduce with stress tool (kvcache reload + high concurrent batch)
- if reproducible, prepare kernel/driver bisect and vendor escalation.

lucy: I'm taking the investigation shift at 09:30 UTC — I'll validate the repro and coordinate the kernel vendor/escalation. priya, handing off final oncall notes.

priya: handing off. summary: cordoned prod-gpu-03, drain in progress, traffic routed to CPU-fallback for impacted models, customers notified, metrics + logs collected. lucy owns next shift and vendor engagement.

incident-bot: HANDOFF recorded — priya -> lucy at 2026-03-17T09:30:00Z.

lucy: noted. I'll also schedule a short rolling patch window for the GPU node pool tonight (low traffic) to either rollback kernel or test updated driver 535.12. will keep updates in this thread.

jamie: thanks. one action item for postmortem: capture exact sequence that causes cuMemAlloc illegal address + any correlation with paging/eviction churn. add a prompt set to Redwood Optimize to catch regressions.

lucy: agreed. adding to the incident timeline + opening postmortem doc. will include the driver/kernel versions and the k8s node lifecyle events.

max: leaving a small log snippet here for the postmortem timeline: `2026-03-17T08:58:11Z pod embedder-v2-7dc crashed: RuntimeError: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`

priya: closing immediate mitigation: node cordoned, affected traces captured, CS notified, fallback in place. monitoring for reoccurrence for 2 hours.

lucy: update 09:58 UTC — drain complete, node isolated. no new OOMs on other nodes after fallback. vendor escalation ticket opened with NVidia (case #NV-88122). will update when vendor responds.

jamie: marking incident as TRIAGED. thanks team. :thumbsup:
